darshana: Nail bed and lip colour -- pallor or cyanosis
Facial complexion (varna) -- pallor, dusky or flushed
Neck veins for visible distension
Ankles and sacrum for visible swelling
Resting breathing effort and posture the patient chooses for comfort
sparshana: Radial and carotid pulse (nadi) -- rate, rhythm, volume, bilateral equality
Skin temperature and moisture of the extremities -- warm/dry vs cold/clammy
Praecordium -- locate and characterise the apex impulse
Ankle and sacral area for pitting oedema
cardiovascular.notes: Pulse character (nadi pariksha) is examined here strictly as a physical-exam finding (rate/rhythm/volume), not as a dosha-diagnostic reading.

darshana: Respiratory rate, rhythm and effort; use of accessory muscles
Chest wall shape and symmetry of movement on breathing
Lips and nail beds for cyanosis
Sputum, if produced -- colour, consistency, quantity
Ability to speak in full sentences without breathlessness
sparshana: Chest wall for tenderness and symmetry of expansion (hands on both sides of chest)
Tactile fremitus over both lung fields
Chest wall warmth in a febrile patient

darshana: Abdominal contour -- distension, visible peristalsis, asymmetry
Tongue coating and moisture (jihva) as a general digestive-status indicator
Skin and sclera for jaundice
Stool character as reported/observed
sparshana: Light and deep palpation of all four quadrants for tenderness, guarding or masses
Kostha (abdominal) warmth and tenderness on palpation
Liver and spleen margins
Rebound tenderness where peritonism is suspected

darshana: Gait, posture, tremor or other involuntary movement
Facial symmetry and speech clarity
Level of alertness and orientation
Eye movements and pupil symmetry
sparshana: Muscle tone and power on passive/active movement
Deep tendon reflexes
Sensation to light touch across the affected area
Muscle bulk for wasting or spasticity

musculoskeletal.srotas: Asthivaha / Sandhivaha / Mamsavaha Srotas (bone, joint, muscle)
darshana: Joint swelling, deformity, redness
Gait and active range of movement
Muscle bulk for wasting or asymmetry between sides
sparshana: Joint warmth, tenderness and effusion
Passive range of motion and end-feel
Tenderness along the muscle/tendon/ligament line

darshana: Limb colour and venous prominence
Ulceration or skin changes over the limb
Swelling or size asymmetry between limbs
sparshana: Peripheral pulses bilaterally (dorsalis pedis, posterior tibial, popliteal as relevant)
Capillary refill time
Temperature asymmetry between limbs
Calf tenderness

darshana: Conjunctival colour, redness, discharge
Pupil size, shape and symmetry; scleral colour
Eyelid swelling, ptosis or lid-margin change
sparshana: Gentle periorbital palpation for tenderness or swelling
Gross globe firmness (very gentle, closed-lid palpation only)

darshana: Throat and tonsils for redness, exudate, swelling
Nasal discharge -- colour and character
Ear canal and tympanic membrane where an otoscope is available
sparshana: Cervical lymph nodes
Sinuses for tenderness on light pressure
Mastoid and pre-auricular region

darshana: Lesion morphology, colour, distribution and margins
Overall skin dryness or oiliness
sparshana: Lesion texture, temperature and tenderness
Induration or fluctuance

darshana: Body habitus and weight distribution
Skin and hair changes; eye signs where relevant (e.g. thyroid)
Neck contour for goitre
sparshana: Thyroid gland size, nodularity, mobility
Skin texture and moisture
Foot sensation where diabetic neuropathy is a concern

darshana: Urine colour/clarity if a sample is available
Flank or suprapubic distension
sparshana: Renal angle tenderness
Suprapubic region for bladder distension/tenderness

darshana: Abdominal contour and pallor
sparshana: Gentle abdominal palpation for tenderness or masses, within the examiner's scope and training
obstetric.notes: Internal/speculum examination is outside the Darshana-Sparshana scope of this checklist and follows standard biomedical protocol only.

darshana: Demeanour, eye contact, psychomotor activity
Speech rate, tone and content
sparshana: Not routinely applicable; pulse rate/character may be noted as a general anxiety correlate only

darshana: Activity level, feeding, hydration signs
Work of breathing and colour
sparshana: Gentle palpation as tolerated by the child
Fontanelle (in infants) for fullness or depression

darshana: Overall nourishment, complexion and hydration status
General build and posture
sparshana: Skin temperature and moisture
A general peripheral pulse check
